notes:
Prospect: mid-market product discovery SaaS targeting SMB+ e-com merchants. Primary interest: improve search relevance by adding an LLM-based reranker after initial retrieval; want to keep initial retrieval lightweight (BM25/ann) and run Redwood rerank endpoint for top-20 results.

Key constraints: latency p95 target ~120-200ms for rerank step (overall search flow ~250ms), throughput ~30-60 qps during peak, cost sensitivity moderate — willing to pay for consistent p95 but wants cost controls and clear unit economics.

POC scope: run hosted rerank endpoint on their labeled eval set (1k queries) to compare baseline (BM25) vs reranked results using NDCG@10/MRR. They will provide gold labels and a small set of A/B prompts. Offline scoring needed for historical logs (replay) to measure lift across segments.

Security: require SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance, audit logs, optional KMS for key management, and EU data residency for a subset of clients (they have EU customers). Asked about Private / Dedicated with VPC and customer keys post-POC.

Model preferences: prefer smaller open models for rerank (cost + inference latency), want Redwood to suggest quantization and batching configs via Optimize. Also asked about fallback policies and multi-model routing when Dedicated capacity constrained.

Quotes/phrases from meeting: 'We can't afford a 400ms tail in searches, even if relevance improves' ; 'If hosted POC shows measurable lift we'll commit to a 12-month reserved pool' ; 'Need clear eval metrics — NDCG and percentage of clicks improved by rerank'.

Next steps/owner: Priya to schedule POC start (this week). Daniel to provide sample POC notebook and rerank endpoint quickstart. Sales to supply Dedicated pricing tiers and example TCO for 50 qps steady-state. Security to follow up on SOC2 evidence and VPC network diagram (linked).

Stated blockers: finance needs annual commitment figures; security wants VPC diagram and KMS details before Dedicated trial. Labeled dataset still being cleaned (estimated 1 week).

Notes style: mixed fragments, action items, and direct quotes — typical CRM entry.
